Fill-in exercise of nine short mini-dialogues practising present-tense forms (affirmative, negative and -ko questions) of verb type 4 and 5 verbs such as siivota, osata, tarvita, lukita, maalata and kerätä.

Newspaper Donald Duck (Aku Ankka) spot-the-difference puzzle: Donald waits by a barbecue to grill a corn cob; find the differences between the two pictures.

Nine photos of health problems (broken arm, back pain, red eye, vomiting, runny nose, headache, sore throat, itchy rash, eye examination) each with two blank lines for the learner to write what is wrong. No printed text; answers are derived.

Children's picture vocabulary page on illness, words split into syllables: symptoms (headache, fever, cough, sore throat, runny nose, stomach ache), health care words (doctor, nurse, patient, medicine, plaster, cast, vaccination), sairas/terve, and verbs sairastaa, parantua, yskiä, niistää, oksentaa; a fox says 'Parane pian!'.

Children's picture vocabulary page (syllabified): 12 body parts and 5 people words, each with its nominative plural (pää – päät, käsi – kädet, jalka – jalat, poika – pojat …); a rabbit says 'Tässä on pää.'

Map of Europe with Finnish names of countries, capitals and seas, plus the model question 'Minkä maan pääkaupunki on Pariisi? – Se on Ranskan pääkaupunki.' A route around European capitals is hand-drawn with arrows and some countries highlighted.
Bilingual picture dictionary page 61 'on the farm': 16 labelled farm animals and objects (haystack, turkey, goose, horse, bull, tractor, goat, pig, hen, field, fence …).
Bilingual picture dictionary page 'maatilalla' (on the farm): a farm scene plus labelled sheep, lamb, cow, calf, duck, ducklings, milk containers, orchard and cockerel.

Grammar box on consonant gradation in nouns: strong → weak pairs (kk→k, pp→p, tt→t, k→–, p→v, t→d, nk→ng, nt→nn, mp→mm, lt→ll, rt→rr) with examples, plus exceptions (sk, st, tk; words ending in two vowels).

Farm-animal vocabulary list (lammas, lehmä, vasikka, ankka, hanhi, kukko, hevonen, vuohi, sika, kana…) where each word heads a sentence with an English phrase in brackets to translate, practising KPT gradation in plurals, local cases, genitive and 'have' (-lla on).
